evidence.finding: All 11 intervals from 09:15 through 11:45 were reported exactly 26.0 points below the formula-based service level; earlier intervals matched.
Multiple post-onset intervals reported more answered than offered calls, including 93 answered versus 90 offered at 10:30.
Post-onset offered volume averaged only 0.18% above forecast, excluding a sustained unexpected-demand surge.
Scheduled and logged-in staffing remained 49; productive staffing stayed at 45–46 and adherence was nearly unchanged.
No routing, platform, or other operational event was recorded during the full incident window.
Localized pressure affected Account Support, but the other three queues maintained post-onset mean service levels of 87.8%–92.1% with unchanged staffing.

primary_root_cause_detail: Beginning exactly at 09:15, the dashboard understated service level by a fixed 26.0 percentage points in every visible interval. Formula-based service level was mostly above target, while post-onset performance records also contained count inconsistencies.
recommended_actions: Correct the dashboard calculation or transformation that introduced the fixed 26-point offset at 09:15.
Backfill affected intervals using the defined service-level formula and validate count-conservation rules.
Add automated alerts for fixed metric offsets and answered-call counts exceeding offered-call counts.
Monitor Account Support during moderate volume increases, while treating its localized pressure separately from the reporting defect.

rejected_hypotheses.reason: Volume increased versus the earlier period but averaged essentially on forecast after onset.
Logged-in headcount was constant, productive staffing was stable, and no training capacity was removed.
Post-onset AHT decreased versus the pre-incident mean and averaged below forecast.
Transfers decreased and no routing event was recorded.
Only localized pressure was visible; staffing was unchanged and most queues remained healthy, so it cannot explain the center-wide fixed metric offset.

stakeholder_summary: The sustained below-target dashboard alert was primarily a reporting error, not a center-wide operational failure. Correct recalculation shows brief genuine dips at 09:15 and 09:45 amid moderate localized pressure, but not the persistent severe decline displayed.
